notes: Breastfeeding: the NHS says ramipril can be taken while breastfeeding but to talk to a doctor or pharmacist first (best avoided if the baby was born prematurely); SPS says use with caution, enalapril preferred. The first-pass claim that some maker leaflets are stricter was not retrieved in this pass, so it was cut; a human may wish to check the current emc leaflets and SmPC. Salt substitutes: 'Lo-Salt' and the NHS attribution were not confirmed; the final text cites MedlinePlus (talk to a doctor before potassium-containing salt substitutes) and UK labelling (salt substitutes listed with potassium supplements for hyperkalaemia). The NHS who-can-and-cannot-take-ramipril page was never returned in 7 searches, so every claim relying on it (most adults, condition list, surgery, diabetes sugar checks) was cut or replaced with labelling statements. Search summaries blend pages, so leaflet-level attributions (pil.10671 vs pil.8066, SmPC 7104 vs 8066) are approximate. Alcohol: two NHS summaries differed in firmness ('not until you see how ramipril affects you' vs 'not too much'); kept the former attributed. Textbook count 2 of 64 (angiotensin II sentence cut; throat swelling kept). Section 4 was renamed. No sentence rated unsafe.
